label: Late-episode D2 reset dip is smaller after reaching S1 or prior reward, larger after choosing a2.
short_terms: (in_state == 1) * ep_dec * ep_dec ;; (phase == D2) * prev_reward * ep_dec ;; (in_action == 2) * ep_dec * ep_dec
terms: (phase == D2) * (state == S1) * ep_dec ** 2 ;; (phase == D2) * prev_reward * ep_dec ** 2 ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * ep_dec ** 2 ;; (phase == D2) * (state == S1) ;; (phase == D2) * prev_reward ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) ;; (phase != D2) * prev_reward * ep_dec ** 2 ;; (phase == D2) * belief_lo * ep_dec
explanation: Raw reset gate r of unit 30 sits near 1 at D1/GO and dips at D2, and the dip deepens sharply late in the episode (timing alone R^2 0.85). Beyond timing, the magnitude is almost entirely a D2 effect whose size grows with episode time, roughly quadratically. At D2 it is higher when the reached state is S1, higher when the previous trial was rewarded, and lower when this trial chose a2. The lowest values are late-episode a2 trials after unrewarded outcomes. These are all observed at D2 (in_state and in_action are D2 inputs), so no future variables are used. D1/GO effects are tiny: a weak negative belief_lo dependence at D1 and lower values at GO after unrewarded trials. The free fit adds the main effects that do not scale with time, plus a belief x episode term at D2. Additive cue tables without episode interactions reach only 0.29, so the interaction with episode time is essential.
